item.title: CISA
item.description:
Certified Information Systems Auditor

Focus: Specialises in information systems auditing—planning and performing audits, evaluating governance and controls, and reporting assurance over IT-enabled business processes and information assets. (ISACA)

Industry: Suits organisations with strong assurance and compliance needs such as government, critical infrastructure, finance, healthcare, large enterprises, and consulting/audit firms. (ISACA)

Requirements

  • Pass the CISA Exam (US$575 ISACA Member, US$760 Non-member)
    • Format: 150 multiple-choice questions, scaled score of 450 or higher (on a 200–800 scale) to pass.
    • Duration: 4 hours.
    • Content:
      • Information System Auditing Process (18%)
      • Governance & Management of IT (18%)
      • Information Systems Acquisition, Development & Implementation (12%)
      • Information Systems Operations and Business Resilience (26%)
      • Protection of Information Assets (26%)
  • Relevant work experience
    • At least five years of professional work experience in information systems auditing, control, assurance, or security.
    • Experience must be within the 10 years preceding the application date, and you must have experience in at least 1 of the 5 CISA job practice domains.
    • You have five years after passing the exam to apply for certification.
    • Experience waivers can reduce the required five years by up to a maximum of three years (for example, via combinations of general IS/audit experience and education waivers).
  • Submit the certification application and pay the US$50 application processing fee.
  • Agree to ISACA’s Code of Professional Ethics and ongoing continuing professional education requirements.

Pete Zerger - YouTube - CISA Exam Prep Playlist (7hrs)

item.title: CRISC
item.description:
Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control

Focus: Specialises in enterprise IT risk management and control. Ideal for those identifying, assessing and mitigating information systems risks.

Industry: Suits industries with strong risk management requirements like insurance, fintech, healthcare and government institutions.

Requirements

Requirements for CRISC certification - Pass the CRISC Exam (US$575 ISACA Member, US$760 Non-member) - Format: 150 multiple-choice questions, scaled score of >450 out of 800 to pass. - Duration: 4 hours. - **Content: - Governance (26%): IT risk governance, frameworks, policies, and organizational structures. - IT Risk Assessment (20%): Risk identification, evaluation, and analysis. - Risk Response and Reporting (32%): Mitigating risk, implementing controls, and communicating results. - Information Technology and Security (22%): Supporting risk management through IT controls and solutions. - Relevant Work Experience - At least three years of cumulative, professional-level work experience in at least two of the four CRISC domains. - At least one year of experience in either IT Risk Identification or IT Risk Assessment - Experience must be verified and within the 10 years preceding the certification application or within five years after passing the exam.

item.title: Pentesting
item.description:
Penetration testing is a process in which a security professional simulates an attack on a network or computer system to evaluate its security—with the permission of that system’s owners AKA ethical hacking, white-hat hacking, red-teaming

  • Becoming a PenTester (Huge resource)
  • PentestBox.org - Open Source Portable PenTest Environment for Windows
  • 8 Common Pentesting mistakes
  • Penetration Testing Execution Standard [HUGE RESOURCE]
  • OWASP Security Testing Guide
  • NIST Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment

TTPs

  • MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Matrix - Full Enterprise ATT&CK Matrix
  • MITRE ATT&CK Navigator - For creating an exportable ATT&CK matrix layer
  • CVE.Org - Vulnerability catalog and reporting

Books

  • 1 - Penetration Testing: A Hands-On Introduction to Hacking eBook: Weidman, Georgia
